cycles.method: An event is one track's render for one 16-sample frame, called by the base in the frame interrupt (two calls when a trig falls inside the frame, split at its sample offset). The budget is the whole frame, the render's deadline: 362.8 us, 47,891 counts of the 132 MHz timer, 95,782 cycles at 264 MHz; the base's guard lets the interrupt use 80 % of it. Measured on the author's MKII, 7 November 2026, with the base's frame guard (npm run device -- do guard) and the per-render timers of a RAM-booted development twin (diag v3, 7bce173d) of his flashed base 86388105, package f501a6a4, 120 s a run, the author playing his live set: the dearest single render was the second call of a frame holding a trig, 37.1 % of the frame (35,536 cycles, a heavy SAW with both detuned pairs, both subs, DRIV, filter and chorus on the track), while no first call of a frame passed 16.2 % (15,517). The same ratio, 1.8 to 2.4, was seen in every run from 3 to 7 November on three bases; its cause was not found (not code size: a build with half the code cost more; not the samples' starts; stock's START is never called on a SYNTIZ track). At the three-track limit three such renders in one frame would sum to 106,608 cycles, above the frame: the guard then drops a render, 16 samples of silence on that track. Three heavy tracks measured together on 31 October (twin 04e94075, same package, each holding a note at its heaviest): 48.2 % of each frame on average over 120 s, 16.1 % a track, 2 renders dropped, longest frame 109.6 %. A static bound is not established: under qemu cfv4e the render executes at most 6,372 instructions (ENS, tools/count_cf.sh), 4,044 for a heavy SAW, but on the unit the same render costs about 2.5 cycles an instruction warm and up to about 8.8 cold (the 37.1 % render).

load.method: The base's frame guard (npm run device -- do guard), not cfmeter.py, on the RAM-booted development twin 7bce173d of the author's MKII base, 7 November 2026, package f501a6a4, the guard's share 80 %: the author's complete live set (T1 THRU, T2-T4 three samples, T5 SAW with both detuned pairs, both subs, filter and chorus, T6 TABLE with filter and chorus, T7 NEIGHBOR with flanger, T8 master compressor), long notes, the author playing it as on stage (STOP/PLAY, scenes, encoders). Without SYNTIZ loaded, the first 15,935 frames of the run: 36.3 % of each frame in the frame interrupt, longest frame 103.7 % (376.2 us: stock's own peaks at transitions). With SYNTIZ on T5 and T6, 344,936 frames: 73.8 %, longest 114.1 % (414.0 us), 259 renders dropped by the guard in 120 s (about two a second, on T5 and T6), the guard's credit exhausted at moments (minimum -2.6 %); the author heard nothing and called it clean. Idle is 100 minus the interrupt's share. The same set with two samples instead of three (his reference set): 69.3 % while playing, longest 111.2 %, 0 renders dropped; the pattern playing alone, 60.3 %, longest 94.5 %, 0 dropped. A render is about 15 % of a frame, so the longest-frame rise and the idle fall are far above the audit's 10 % rule: the owner's decision is asked for in the release pull request.

stress.droppedExplanation: No MIDI flood ran: SYNTIZ has no MIDI path of its own, MIDI notes reach it through the track's PTCH as for FLEX, and nothing on the author's computer sends MIDI to the unit yet. Its stress run is the author's live set above, played for 120 s with STOP/PLAY, scenes and encoders: no hang, no stuck note heard. A flood is still to run.
